title: Access, Pins, Limits and Pricing
snippet:
Pinterest's API v5 creates Pins on a user's boards with POST /pins and the pins:write scope, and lists no fee. New apps get Trial access, usually in 1 to 3 business days, but every Pin and board created on Trial is visible only to its creator. Public Pins need Standard access, which takes a demo video and a review with no stated duration.

PricePinterest lists no fee. The tiers are Trial and Standard access
Trial accessRequested in the developer portal, usually approved in 1 to 3 business days. Pins and boards created on Trial are visible only to their creator
Standard accessAn upgrade request with a video of your app's OAuth flow and an API action. No stated review time
Scopesboards:read, boards:write, pins:read and pins:write
Write limit300 a day per app on Trial; 100 a minute per user on Standard
Access tokens30 days. Continuous refresh tokens last 60 days and renew each time they're used
Your accountThe developer needs a Pinterest business account to run the app
Checked on October 6, 2026, from Pinterest's developer documentation and terms.
## How to get access to the Pinterest APIFrom a developer account to your first real post.
1. 1Use a business accountLog in to developers.pinterest.com with a Pinterest business account, verify its email and accept the Developer Terms.
2. 2Connect an app and request Trial accessRequests are reviewed every business day, and approval typically takes 1 to 3 business days, by email. The app id and secret then show under My apps.
3. 3Build on TrialUp to 1,000 requests a day per app, 300 of them writes. Everything you create is visible only to you, and the sandbox can't create video Pins.
4. 4Upgrade to StandardFrom the app card: a video of your app taking users through OAuth and completing an action with the API. Requests are reviewed regularly, with no stated duration.

## Is the Pinterest API free?
Pinterest's developer docs list no fee or paid tier: the only tiers are Trial and Standard access.
What costs is Standard access. Until you have it, nothing you post is public, and the upgrade needs a finished app and a demo video.

title: Pinterest API Pricing: Complete Guide for 2026
snippet:
The headline is short: Pinterest does not publish API access fees for v5. No price card, no per-call meter, no subscription fee.

| Access tier | Cost | Best for | Key friction |
|---|---|---|---|
| Trial access (v5) | Free | Building and testing against a sandbox before launch | Universal cap of 1,000 req/day per app across all endpoints, with `ads_write` stricter at 300/day. Pins are hidden from the public. Product-limited test tokens expire after 24 hours |
| Standard access (v5) | Free | Production publishing, ads, catalogs, analytics | Manual review of a video demo, approval criteria are not published as a fixed checklist |
| Marketing Developer Partners (MDP) | Not publicly priced. Limited, curated program. | Software companies publishing on behalf of brands at scale | Pinterest’s own description calls MDP a “limited, carefully selected group of developer partners” |
| Ads API (inside v5, Standard tier) | Free | Building and reporting on Pinterest ad campaigns at scale | Standard access required, must comply with the developer guidelines’ fee-disclosure rules |
| Third-party read APIs (Bright Data, scraper services) | Pricing varies by vendor and volume | Off-platform research, competitive data, public-pin discovery at scale | Outside Pinterest’s terms in many cases, check each vendor’s compliance posture before you build on top |

The current [rate limits page](https://developers.pinterest.com/docs/reference/rate-limits/) lists them per category, in plain numbers. `ads_read` and `org_read` sit at 1,000 requests/minute per user per app. `ads_write` sits at 400. `advanced_auction_write` sits at 25. `ads_conversions` is the outlier at 120,000 per ad account per minute. The shape of your integration (mostly reads, mostly writes, mostly bidding actions) decides whether you can run on Standard at all or whether you need a partner conversation.

### Trial access (Free)
Pinterest hands every approved developer Trial access after the first review. The point of Trial is to let you call real endpoints with a real OAuth token before you ship.
You get the full endpoint surface (pins, boards, ads, catalogs, analytics, trends) at per-category caps. Test tokens expire after 24 hours, which is the right design for a sandbox and the wrong shape for testing a multi-day workflow.

title: Pinterest API: pins, boards and the approval you need first
snippet:
Two tiers, no others. From Pinterest's [access tiers guide](https://developers.pinterest.com/docs/key-concepts/access-tiers/), read today:
| | Trial | Standard |
|---|---|---|
| Positioning | "best for exploring our API features" | "get the full functionality that our API offers" |
| Can read and create | ads, audiences, boards, Pins, catalogs | same |
| Visibility of what you create | boards and Pins visible only to their creator | normal public visibility |
| Rate limit window | daily, per app | per minute, per user, per app |
| All API requests | 1,000 per day | 100 per second per user per app |
| Organic reads (`org_read`) | 1,000 per day | 1,000 per minute |
| Organic writes (`org_write`) | 300 per day | 100 per minute |
| Ads reads (`ads_read`) | 1,000 per day | 1,000 per minute |
| Ads writes (`ads_write`) | 300 per day | 400 per minute |

To move up: the app must already be approved for Trial and comply with the Developer Guidelines, and you submit a video of your app completing an action with the Pinterest API that shows the OAuth flow. That applies even if you are the only user, and terminal or Postman screen recordings are accepted. Pinterest verifies your use case and your privacy policy link during submission. You go to My apps, select **Upgrade** on the app card, confirm the information, upload the video, submit. There is no published timeline: requests are "reviewed regularly" and you get an email with the decision. If it is denied and you appeal through a Help Center ticket, allow "a few days".

Three grants, and only one of them gives you the whole API:
- **Authorization Code**, for acting on a user's behalf. The user approves scopes at `https://www.pinterest.com/oauth/`, lands back on your `redirect_uri` with a code, and your server exchanges it at `oauth/token`. This is the only grant with full API coverage.
- **Client Credentials**, for your own developer account. It requires two-factor authentication and cannot reach some sensitive endpoints.
- **Refresh Token**, to swap a refresh token for a fresh access token with no user involved.
The authorize call wants `client_id`, `redirect_uri`, `response_type=code` and `scope`. `state` is optional and you should send it anyway, since it is what protects the callback from cross-site request forgery.

Pinterest publishes no price for API access: the tiers and these limits are the rationing.

snippet: The Pinterest API v5 significantly increases the scope of what is possible for you to create as a developer. If approved for API use, your app receives Trial access, which is best for exploring our API features. If you want to offer Pinterest capabilities to your users, we recommend upgrading to Standard access to get the full functionality that our API offers.

title: Pinterest Developers
snippet:
There are a few steps you need to take in order to connect your first app.
1. Login or [create a business account](https://help.pinterest.com/business/article/create-an-advertiser-account). This is the account you will use to administer your app.
2. Verify your account's email address
3. Go to [**My apps**](/apps/) and click through to accept our Developer Terms of Service

1. Select **Connect app** and complete our request form with your app information. Your app name can be in any language, but it must include at least 3 Latin letters or numbers (A-Z, a-z, 0-9) and can't contain the word "Pinterest".
2. Submit your request for trial access.
Application requests are reviewed by Pinterest. You will receive an email notification after your app has been reviewed, letting you know whether it was approved or denied access.
If your app is approved for [Trial access](/docs/key-concepts/access-tiers/), you can log into your account and manage your app details on your My apps page. In your My apps view, you'll be able to find details such as your unique app ID and app secret.
[Review our guide on access tiers](/docs/key-concepts/access-tiers/) for more details on the application process and what to expect with each level of access.

title: Pinterest API alternative: public pins, boards and search without app approval
snippet:
Slowly. According to Pinterest's [guide to connecting a developer app](https://developers.pinterest.com/docs/getting-started/connect-app/), you:
1. Log in with (or create) a Pinterest business account and verify its email.
2. Accept the Developer Terms of Service under My apps.
3. Submit a "Connect app" request form, which Pinterest reviews and answers by email.
4. Request Trial access, and only after approval see your app ID and secret.
5. Register a redirect URI and implement the OAuth 2 flow to get and refresh access tokens.
Then comes Trial access. Pinterest's [access tiers page](https://developers.pinterest.com/docs/key-concepts/access-tiers/) says "all Pins and Boards created with Trial access are only visible to their creator as Sandbox entities", and "Apps with Trial access are rate limited based on calls per day/per app."
To move up to Standard access you record a video of your app completing an action through the API. Solo developers don't get a pass: "If you are the only intended user of the Pinterest API, we will still require a video recording of the OAuth flow."
Is the API free? Pinterest's docs don't list a per-call fee for v5, so you pay in time instead: the review, the OAuth build and the video. Fair for a scheduling tool. A lot of paperwork for "what do the top 50 pins for *linen bedding* link to?"
